This guide computes the two-port S-parameters of the CPW from
[AEDT inputs from a GDS file](aedt-inputs.qmd), in the same Python session.
Driven Terminal ports name their **reference conductors** explicitly, instead
of using an integration line as [Driven Modal](aedt-driven-modal.qmd) does.
The two port models are different, even if their curves look similar.

## Set up and prepare the run

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import (
    FrequencySweepSpec, HfssDrivenSpec, HfssRunControl, LengthMeshSpec,
    TerminalPort, prepare_handoff,
)

ports = (
    TerminalPort(1, "o1", "-X", ground_objects),
    TerminalPort(2, "o2", "+X", ground_objects),
)
spec = HfssDrivenSpec(
    mode="terminal", gds_path=source_gds, modeling="thin_film",
    project_name="cpw_terminal", design_name="CpwFiniteGroundTerminal",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    layer_imports=layer_imports, object_bindings=object_bindings,
    physical_layers=(physical_layer,),
    ports=ports,
    run_control=HfssRunControl(
        "Setup1", "Fast20000", FrequencySweepSpec(3.0, 8.0, 20_000)
    ),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
    length_mesh=LengthMeshSpec(("D0_TOP_M1_1",), ground_objects, 10.0),
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/cpw-terminal"))
print(handoff.run_dir)
```

- `TerminalPort(number, name, face, references)` places a wave port on a face
  of the vacuum region. `references` names the ground objects,
  `("D0_TOP_M1_2", "D0_TOP_M1_3")`. SCGSim does not guess a reference from
  touching geometry.
- `TerminalPort` also accepts `deembed_um`, a nonnegative de-embedding
  distance in micrometres; the default is zero.
- The sweep, padding and mesh settings are the same as in
  [Driven Modal](aedt-driven-modal.qmd#set-up-and-prepare-the-run).

### Lumped terminal ports

For a lumped port inside the model instead of a wave port on a face, use
`LumpedTerminalPort`. It needs an explicit sheet, signal and reference
conductors, and `impedance_ohm`. The [runtime reference](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#hfss-shared-lumped-support)
describes it.

A port impedance is not a circuit element. For a linear RLC element in an
Eigenmode model, see [HFSS Eigenmode](aedt-eigenmode.qmd#add-a-lumped-rlc-element-optional).

## Run and read the result

[Run the directory](execute.qmd), then [load it](returned-results.qmd):

```python
from scgsim.aedt import resolve_results

result = resolve_results(".artifacts/cpw-terminal")
result.show_all_results()
```

The result contains the S-parameters in port order and a Touchstone file.
SCGSim checks after the run that AEDT assigned the references you named.
